doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ohio, Cleveland tenor players and Buffalo vocal groups
summary: Fuller recalls Mel Wanzo in Ohio, a Cleveland tenor called Joe, Grant Green and the Burrell family, and Hendricks's brother's group in Buffalo.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: We don’t need to spend a lot of time on this but, Detroit, Toledo, how much Ohio did you get into?
Quite a bit. Remember, I had been with Mel Wanzo so and we did a lot of practicing together.
He’s out of Daton?
No, he’s out of Warren Ohio. Then, there was a guy in Cleveland, a big boy, Joe Green, or something.
You talking about the tenor player?
Yeah.
He’s like a legend.
Yeah.
We came up on—maybe it wasn’t this one—I want to say Carter? No…Joe. Because, I know Joe Lovano’s father, he talks about him. He was the cat.

He was the cat. He was a big guy. He looked like George Colon. I can’t think of his name. Then there was another guy they called Popeye. He had another name. He did some dates around with some good people. He was still lingering with the other stuff.
Was there a relationship between Detroit and Buffalo or Detroit and Chicago on a sort of… Cities on the Great Lakes?

I don’t know but I know John Hendricks’s brother went out to Buffalo to start a group like his brother. When I went up there, with all the guys there, they were singing similar songs. Pabon, that girl named Pabon?
Yolanda Pabon?
She was actually singing with the brother in Buffalo and then she joined the group.
Why can’t I remember this tenor player’s name? That’s can on me the rest of this tape.
I know it’s Joe but it wasn’t Green.
I think it’s Carter.

It could have been Carter. He was from Cleveland. There was an alto player that was better than him but he refused to leave. He had a big family. Like, Grant Green didn’t want to come to New York, he was milkman. The real start in Kenny Burrell’s family was Bill Burrell.
What did he play?
Guitar. And he ended up lucrative jobs do those things on the bass, and he was a guitar player, a handsome guy.
